title: Canonicalize the Supabase projection contract for quirk-os-alpha
desired_change: Add version-controlled Supabase migrations and projection contracts for tribunal runs and Proposed Moves; record source repository, PR, commit, content hash, canonical state, and rebuild cursor; keep tables in a private schema, revoke public roles, enable RLS as defense in depth, run advisors, and document rebuild/drift/forgetting procedures.
expected_outcome: The existing Supabase runtime becomes an inspectable projection of Git-backed proposed state rather than hidden infrastructure or silent canon.

risk.rights_or_safety_impact: A database projection can expose sensitive move content or silently become authoritative.

hidden_context_dependencies: An active quirk-os-alpha Supabase project exists but the PR does not mention its project ref, current migrations, schemas, or tables.
The repository has no Supabase migration directory or projection schema.
No source commit/hash fields prove which Git state a row projects.
No RLS/grant/exposure policy is documented for new queue tables.
No rebuild, drift, backup, retention, or forgetting procedure exists.
Existing remote schema changes and repository migration history are not reconciled.
acceptance_checks: Migration is present in Git and applied once to quirk-os-alpha.
Tables live in a non-exposed schema with no anon/authenticated grants and RLS enabled.
Every projected row carries source commit, content hash, canonical state, and source path.
Security and performance advisors show no unresolved tribunal-created finding.
Projection rebuild and deletion/forgetting are tested.
